牙.meaning: A long curved tooth juts sideways out of a beast's jaw, with a hook at the root and a sharp slash at the tip. The beast tosses its head and the tooth flashes white in the sun. That's a <kanji>tusk</kanji>.
牙.on: A tiny <sound>ge</sound>cko clings to the tip of the tusk and enjoys the ride.
牙.kun: An elephant hangs its <sound>key</sound>s on its tusk, and a passing sheep bleats '<sound>Bah</sound>!'

邪.meaning: A villain sticks a sharp <part>tusk</part> on the end of his flagpole and flies a black <part>pennant</part> beneath it. He steals sweets from children and laughs as he marches by. Truly <kanji>wicked</kanji>.
邪.on: He hides all the stolen sweets in a big glass <sound>ja</sound>r.
邪.kun: He swaps your <sound>yo</sound>gurt for glue, hides a <sound>ko</sound>ala in your bed and paints your <sound>shee</sound>p green.

初.meaning: A young knight draws a <part>sword</part> and gives it a swing. Clang! It knocks the <part>weathervane</part> clean off the roof. Everyone gasps, then forgives him: it's his <kanji>first time</kanji>.
初.on: He buys a new weathervane at a little <sound>sho</sound>p down the lane.
初.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' laugh his friends, and they drive him home in a <sound>jee</sound>p.

老.meaning: Long ago he threw a javelin so far that it's still out there, a <part>stuck javelin</part> in the field. Now he sits beside it, slurping soup from a <part>spoon</part> and telling the story again. He's an <kanji>old man</kanji> now.
老.on: Every year he plants a red <sound>ro</sound>se beside the javelin.
老.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>, my knees,' he sighs, getting up from his chair a little slower each year.

末.meaning: A <part>tree</part> grows so tall that a <part>one</part>-plank sign is nailed across its very top: no further. A squirrel climbs up, reads it, looks at the sky and sits down. This is the <kanji>end</kanji> of the tree.
末.on: At the end of the day, <sound>Ma</sound>ma squirrel rides home on a <sound>tsu</sound>nami of falling leaves.
末.kun: She ends her day with <sound>su</sound>shi and a boiled <sound>e</sound>gg.

始.meaning: A <part>woman</part> climbs onto a <part>pedestal</part>, lifts a starter's pistol and fires. Bang! Hundreds of runners dash off down the road. She's the one who makes the race <kanji>begin</kanji>.
始.on: Instead of a flag, she waves a knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld to start them off.
始.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' she laughs, as one runner yells '<sound>Gee</sound>, it's started!' and is still tying his shoes.

団.meaning: Inside a big <part>cage</part>, a whole crowd of golfers squeezes in together, each one swinging a <part>golf club</part>. They wear matching shirts and cheer as one. Nobody plays alone here: they're a <kanji>group</kanji>.
団.on: The cage is deep in a <sound>dun</sound>geon, so they practise in the dark.
団.kun: In the dark they bump into a <sound>ca</sound>rp, a <sound>ta</sound>co, a <sound>ma</sound>ma bear and a <sound>ree</sound>f shark, and all huddle into one ball: a lump.

神.meaning: At night a <part>lamppost</part> lights up a strange <part>monkey sign</part> hung in the clouds, a box with a stake through its middle. Lightning crackles from it and a booming voice laughs. It belongs to the <kanji>gods</kanji>.
神.on: One of the gods trips over the lamppost and bangs a <sound>shin</sound>.
神.kun: Up on a cloud, the gods' cat lies <sound>ca</sound>lm and gives a long '<sound>Mee</sound>-ow.'

失.meaning: A <part>husband</part> is carrying the wedding ring up the aisle when a <part>slash</part> of wind knocks it out of his hand. It bounces once, twice, and drops down a drain. Gone. He's managed to <kanji>lose</kanji> it.
失.on: He searches under every bed <sound>shee</sound>t in the house, just in case.
失.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>!' he wails, a <sound>shee</sound>p bleats, and his <sound>na</sound>an goes cold while he looks.

治.meaning: A queen stands on a <part>pedestal</part> in the middle of a wild river and lifts her hand. The <part>water drops</part> stop splashing, the waves lie flat and the floods go home. Now she will <kanji>reign</kanji> over the river.
治.on: Her royal guard is a <sound>chee</sound>tah that runs laps around the pedestal.
治.kun: A sick goat nibbles a <sound>na</sound>an from her hand, then jumps up: '<sound>Oh</sound>! I'm better!'

調.meaning: Before his <part>speech</part>, a singer runs one <part>lap</part> of the stage, plucking each string of his guitar and twisting the pegs as he goes. Too sharp, too flat, just right. He has to <kanji>tune</kanji> it first.
調.on: His tight <sound>cho</sound>ker squeaks every time he hits a high note.
調.kun: A <sound>shee</sound>p in a detective hat inspects every string, then cheers '<sound>Rah</sound>!'

呂.meaning: Two <part>mouth</part> boxes stack one on top of the other, joined by a tiny <part>slash</part> of a link, like two bones in your back. Add more and more, and you can bend and twist: it's a <kanji>spine</kanji>.
呂.on: A <sound>ro</sound>dent climbs your back, bone by bone, like a ladder.
呂.kun: A <sound>se</sound>tter dog walks the length of your back and plants a <sound>bo</sound>nsai at the top, beside a fishing <sound>ne</sound>t.

険.meaning: A <part>campsite</part> clings to a cliff edge, tents pegged onto a narrow ledge, and a <part>pennant</part> flaps from a pole hammered into the rock. Look down: a sheer drop. The path up was <kanji>precipitous</kanji>.
険.on: A dog <sound>ken</sound>nel sits on the very edge, swaying in the wind.
険.kun: A <sound>ke</sound>ttle slides off the ledge, and all the campers cry '<sound>Wah</sound>!'

保.meaning: A little girl hangs her coat on a <part>coat hook</part> and holds up a giant <part>lollipop</part>. Her big brother stands in front of her, arms out, glaring at the seagulls. He's there to <kanji>protect</kanji> it.
保.on: So a seagull snatches his <sound>ho</sound>tdog instead.
保.kun: He keeps the lollipop in a <sound>ta</sound>co box, with a <sound>mo</sound>le on guard.

片.meaning: Saw a log down the middle and keep only the left half. It has a post and a couple of stubby branches sticking out one way, and nothing at all on the other side. A lopsided, <kanji>one-sided</kanji> piece.
片.on: A <sound>hen</sound> perches on the end, and the whole thing tips over to one side.
片.kun: You buy a one-way ticket from a <sound>ca</sound>lm man selling <sound>ta</sound>cos.

悪.meaning: A grumpy giant stomps across a huge map of <part>asia</part> painted on the school floor, smudging every river and mountain, then treads on a paper <part>heart</part> a child made. Nobody likes him. He's simply <kanji>bad</kanji>.
悪.on: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' cries a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo, as the giant stomps on its clock too.
悪.kun: '<sound>Wah</sound>!' the child sobs, and a kanga<sound>roo</sound> boxes the giant on the nose.

千.meaning: A <part>ten</part> stands in the field like a scarecrow, and a crow lands on its head with a <part>slash</part> of wings. Ten crows, then a hundred, then wave after wave until you lose count: one <kanji>thousand</kanji>.
千.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try counts them one by one through his telescope.
千.kun: Then a <sound>chee</sound>tah leaps out of the grass and scatters them all.

具.meaning: A big <part>eye</part> sits above a shelf of <part>one</part> plank, propped on two legs spread like an <part>eight</part>. It watches over the hammers, saws and screwdrivers hung below. Every <kanji>tool</kanji> is in its place.
具.on: Each new apprentice gets a <sound>goo</sound>die bag stuffed with tools.
具.kun: You pack the tools beside a <sound>so</sound>fa and a stack of <sound>na</sound>an, ready for anything: to prepare.

鳥.meaning: A tall head with one bright eye, a long body tipped forward, and four little feet hopping on <part>hot coals</part>. Ouch, ouch, ouch! It flaps its wings and flies off: a <kanji>bird</kanji>.
鳥.on: It lands on a lady's <sound>cho</sound>ker and hangs on by its toes.
鳥.kun: Then it flies to the top of a <sound>to</sound>tem pole, and on out over a coral <sound>ree</sound>f.

了.meaning: On the last day, a builder hangs his <part>crowbar</part> from a <part>one</part>-plank beam. No more prying, no more nails. He wipes his hands, steps back and nods: the job is <kanji>complete</kanji>.
了.on: He celebrates with a long, hot soak at a <sound>ryo</sound>kan.

爪.meaning: A curved hook comes down from above with three sharp prongs hanging under it, spreading wide. It scrapes the floor, snags your sock and won't let go. That's a <kanji>claw</kanji>.
爪.on: It grabs a bar of <sound>soa</sound>p, which squirts straight out of its grip.
爪.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' sneezes the cat, and its claw spears a <sound>me</sound>lon.

受.meaning: A <part>claw</part> reaches down from above, holding out a warm <part>blanket</part>. Below, a hand twisted like a <part>pretzel</part> reaches up and takes it. 'Thank you,' it says. Some gifts you just <kanji>accept</kanji>.
受.on: The whole <sound>ju</sound>ry claps as the blanket is handed down.
受.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>!' you coo, wrapping yourself up in the blanket you just received.

暖.meaning: An arcade <part>claw machine</part> sits out in the <part>sun</part>. You drop in a coin, and the claw grabs not a teddy but a ray of sunshine, and drops it in your lap. You glow all over with <kanji>warmth</kanji>.
暖.on: Carry that sunshine down into a damp <sound>dun</sound>geon, and even the rats cuddle up to it.
暖.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' sigh the rats, toasting a <sound>ta</sound>co in the sunbeam, then a second <sound>ta</sound>co.

校.meaning: Under a big <part>tree</part>, children from every street <part>mingle</part>: they swap snacks and chase each other, then line up when the bell rings. The tree's shade is the classroom. It's a <kanji>school</kanji>.
校.on: At break time, everyone gets an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne.

良.meaning: A <part>robot</part> wakes up with a shiny dot of light on its head. It washes the dishes, walks the dog and helps an old lady across the road. The light glows green: <kanji>good</kanji>.
良.on: As a reward, the robot gets a night at a <sound>ryo</sound>kan, with slippers on all its feet.
良.kun: It even shares its <sound>yo</sound>gurt with the dog. Good robot.

素.meaning: A curious kid takes apart a <part>TV antenna</part> and a spool of <part>thread</part> to see what's inside: just wire, just fluff. The plainest bits that things are made of, lesson one: <kanji>elementary</kanji>.
素.on: She lays all the bare bits out on a squashy <sound>so</sound>fa.
素.kun: Then she builds them back up from the bottom: a <sound>mo</sound>le hill first, a <sound>to</sound>tem pole on top. Back to the source.

改.meaning: A grumpy <part>cobra</part> hisses at everyone, until a teacher sits it down and waves a <part>fan</part> under its nose, day after day, lesson after lesson. Now it says please and thank you. What a <kanji>reformation</kanji>.
改.on: To celebrate, the cobra flies a <sound>ki</sound>te with a smiley face on it.
改.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' gasp its friends, '<sound>Rah</sound>-rah!' cheer the snakes, and the new cobra bows over a plate of <sound>ta</sound>cos.

防.meaning: Pirates swing a big <part>sail</part> toward your castle, but you wave a <part>pennant</part> from the tower and every archer fires at once. The ship turns and flees. You've managed to <kanji>ward off</kanji> the attack.
防.on: Just to be safe, you roll a <sound>bou</sound>lder in front of the gate.
防.kun: You keep out the pirates, their <sound>foo</sound>d and their <sound>se</sound>tter dog.

礼.meaning: Under a <part>lamppost</part>, a soldier snaps his arm up in a sharp <part>zigzag</part>: elbow out, hand to brow. The lamppost flickers its light back at him. Every night they <kanji>salute</kanji> each other.
礼.on: A gliding <sound>ray</sound> in the puddle below lifts one fin to salute too.

居.meaning: An <part>old</part> woman plants a <part>flag</part> on the roof of a tiny house and moves in with her cat. She has no plans to leave, ever. This is where she will <kanji>reside</kanji>.
居.on: She runs a little <sound>kio</sound>sk at the front door, selling tea.
居.kun: She keeps an <sound>ee</sound>l in the bath, and it's there to stay too.
